title: 🔄 Synonyms & Paraphrasing

sections.heading: Why paraphrasing matters
sections.body:
Paraphrasing is the single most important writing skill for IELTS:
• Introduction: You MUST paraphrase the question — never copy
• Task 1: Paraphrase the task description
• Academic Writing: Avoids repetition, shows Lexical Resource
• Reading: Questions paraphrase the passage — you must recognise it

Copying the question word-for-word = ZERO marks for that part.

sections.heading: How to paraphrase
sections.body:
Three techniques:
1. Synonyms: "important" → "significant / crucial / vital"
2. Change word class: "improve" (verb) → "improvement" (noun)
3. Restructure: "Technology has changed society" → "Society has been transformed by technology"

Best paraphrasing uses ALL THREE techniques together.

highlight: A paraphrase should convey the SAME meaning in DIFFERENT words. Changing just one word is not enough — change the structure AND the vocabulary.

example.wrong: "Some people think that technology is beneficial for education." → "Some people believe that technology is good for education."
example.right: "Some people think that technology is beneficial for education." → "There is a widely held view that digital tools have the potential to significantly enhance the learning experience."

sentence: The task prompt says "important." Which word is the BEST academic synonym to use instead?
explanation:
"Significant" is the most versatile academic synonym for "important":
• "a significant impact"
• "a significant increase"
• "significant implications"

Other options:
"Crucial" = absolutely essential
"Vital" = critical for survival
"Paramount" = most important of all (strongest)

"Big", "great", "nice" are informal — avoid in academic writing.

sentence: IELTS question: "The graph shows how many people use public transport." Your introduction should say: "The _______ illustrates the _______ of public transport users."
explanation:
Paraphrase:
• "graph" → "chart" (same type of visual, different word)
• "how many people use" → "the number of users" (change structure)

"Amount" is for uncountable nouns (an amount of water). "Number" is for countable (a number of people). This is a very common error in Task 1.

instruction: Match each common word to its best academic paraphrase:
explanation: These four word families cover a huge proportion of IELTS tasks. Having 3–4 options for each means you never repeat yourself.

question: Which introduction best paraphrases: "Some people believe that governments should spend more money on the arts."?
options: Some people think governments should spend more on arts.
There are people who say governments need to give more money to art.
There exists a school of thought that national governments have an obligation to substantially increase public funding allocated to artistic and cultural endeavours.
Some people believe that governments should invest more money in the arts.
correct: There exists a school of thought that national governments have an obligation to substantially increase public funding allocated to artistic and cultural endeavours.
explanation:
✅ Best paraphrase analysis:
• "Some people believe" → "There exists a school of thought"
• "governments" → "national governments"
• "spend more money on" → "substantially increase public funding allocated to"
• "the arts" → "artistic and cultural endeavours"

Every element is changed using synonyms, class-changes, and restructuring.
